solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Give medal to Grace?

blocks.note: what the army does to a brave soldier
the verb, as flowers grace a table by adorning it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grace' reads as a woman's name, perhaps the medal winner; here it is the verb meaning adorn, so both halves are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one verb: the military one of honouring with a medal, and the ordinary one of adorning.

clue.text: Why you couldn’t get an answer last time?

definitions.text: Why you couldn’t get an answer last time?

blocks.clueFragment: Why you couldn’t get an answer
blocks.note: read as a telephone problem: the connection had failed when you rang
read as the final moment by which an answer must be in

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as DEAD LINE and it explains the unanswered call; read whole, it is the last time allowed for handing something in.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: the clue describes the phone-line reading of the word while quietly pointing at its everyday sense of a cut-off time.

clue.text: Boast about new musician, one who will succeed

blocks.note: to crow is to boast
N is the standard abbreviation for new
Prince, the American singer and guitarist

explanation.surface: Someone brags about a promising new musician tipped for success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' means only 'concerning' here and does not reverse or wrap anything. 'Succeed' is not 'do well' but 'take over the throne'.
explanation.definitionFit: The heir apparent is, by definition, the one who will succeed the monarch.

clue.text: Restore Main Street, foolishly wasting millions

indicators.note: Main Street wastes, or throws away, its M for millions before the letters are rearranged
letters treated foolishly end up in a senseless order

blocks.note: anagram fodder before the deletion
M is the abbreviation for million(s); it is removed

explanation.surface: A town council foolishly squanders millions restoring its high street.
explanation.walkthrough: The M comes out before the shuffle, leaving exactly nine letters for a nine-letter answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to put a person or thing back in its former place.

clue.text: Letter from ambassador at heart of Times article

indicators.note: the ambassador sits at the centre of the two Ts, with the Ts round him

blocks.note: T is time, so times is two Ts, as pages is PP
HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A letter from an ambassador is the centrepiece of an article in The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it is the plural of the abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the answer is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Item left in car

indicators.note: the L is placed in the car

blocks.note: a coupé is a two-door car
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone left a belonging behind in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Item' looks like an object left behind, but it is the informal word for two people in a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: two people romantically linked are said to be 'an item'.

clue.text: Hate old allegations coming back to bite one

indicators.note: the allegations come back, so their word is read in the other direction
the reversed word bites on the one, holding it in its jaws

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
damaging allegations, as in mud-slinging
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Old accusations return to haunt someone and they feel hated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mud' for smears is the step to see: the surface's allegations coming back to bite is exactly what mud does.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: the noun means general hatred or loathing.

clue.text: Kitty weed in sink

blocks.note: the pool of stakes in a card game
slang for cannabis
what a snooker player does to a ball

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions in three words, none of them the obvious reading: not a cat, not a garden plant, not a kitchen basin.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one short word: a pool of money, a drug in slang, and a snooker verb.

clue.text: Requiem for one inhabiting cathedral city

indicators.note: to inhabit a place is to live inside it, so the example word must sit within the city's letters

blocks.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England
e.g. means for example, for one

explanation.surface: A requiem is sung for someone who lived in a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For one' reads like 'for a person', but it is e.g., 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: both are mournful compositions for the dead, one a poem or song, the other a Mass.

clue.text: Clergyman beginning to rush, always on edge

indicators.note: only the beginning of 'rush' is wanted

blocks.note: the first letter of rush
ever = always
an end is an edge or extremity

explanation.surface: A clergyman is starting to hurry and is permanently on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On edge' reads as nervous, but in a down clue 'on' just stacks one piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: The title used as a noun: informally, a reverend is a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Worry past is constraining north European

indicators.note: AGO and IS together hold N between them

blocks.note: ago = in the past
N is the abbreviation for north
used as it stands
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian is held back by anxiety about their past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North European' reads as one idea, a Scandinavian, but it splits: north goes inside the wordplay and European comes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A stronger synonym: to fret or worry intensely over something.

clue.text: Letter from desperate elites clinging to power

indicators.note: the elites are in a desperate, disordered state
the rearranged elites cling round the P

blocks.note: anagram fodder
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A desperate ruling class writes a letter as it clings to power.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's clinging to power is literal: the jumbled elites wrap round the symbol for power.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal or literary word for a letter, as in the New Testament epistles.

clue.text: Nothing initially in boy’s head but painting

indicators.note: only the initial letter of 'nothing' is taken
'in' taken literally as inside: the initial letter is placed within the word for the boy's

blocks.note: a lad is a boy; lad's gives LADS
the first letter of nothing
a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: A boy's mind is empty of everything except painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' is not the top of the body but a headland jutting into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a landscape is one kind of painting, of countryside scenery.

clue.text: Language complaint board ultimately rejected

indicators.note: only the last letter of 'board' is used
that D is rejected, thrown out of the complaint

blocks.note: a malady is an illness, a complaint
the last letter of board, removed

explanation.surface: A complaint about language is finally thrown out by the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' looks like a grievance lodged with a board, but it is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the national language of Malaysia, one language among many.

clue.text: Auntie longs to cook a bit of seafood

indicators.note: cooking the letters mixes them up

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

explanation.surface: An aunt is keen to cook some seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: The cooking fits the seafood so well that 'to cook' passes for part of the story rather than an instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a small lobster-like shellfish, one item of seafood.

clue.text: Line missing from ordinary opera

indicators.note: the L is missing from the word for ordinary

blocks.note: normal = ordinary
L is the abbreviation for line; it is removed

explanation.surface: A line has been cut from an unremarkable opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordinary opera' reads as a critic's jibe, but 'ordinary' is the wordplay and 'opera' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Bellini's opera of 1831, named after its druid priestess heroine.

clue.text: General’s son in tears

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to be in tears is to be weeping

explanation.surface: A military general's son is crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' is the adjective, not the army officer, and 'General's' is 'General is': the definition is followed by the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in one sense: a sweeping statement is a broad, general one.

clue.text: Day I rebel results in ridicule

blocks.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday
used as it stands
to rise up is to rebel

explanation.surface: Someone's day of rebellion only earns them mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Day' is a weekday abbreviation, and 'rebel' is the verb, to rise up.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to mock someone, specifically through satire.

clue.text: Call about crime in priest’s accommodation

indicators.note: the call goes round about the crime

blocks.note: to page someone is to call them
arson is a crime

explanation.surface: Someone phones about a crime at the vicar's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call' is not a phone call but a page, as over a hotel loudspeaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the house a parish provides for its parson, a priest.

clue.text: Record judge defending second hanging

indicators.note: the record and the judge guard the S on either side

blocks.note: to tape is to record
S is the abbreviation for second
to try a case is to judge it

explanation.surface: A judge on record as defending a second hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging' suggests the gallows alongside a judge, but it is a wall hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a woven picture hung on a wall is one kind of hanging.

clue.text: Somehow Enid gets taken in

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged somehow or other

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: Enid has been fooled by some trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets' does double duty as the verb in the surface, and part of the fodder with 'Enid'. 'Taken in' is not fooled but swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in its literal sense: swallowed, taken into the body.

clue.text: Ontario janitor knocking back the red?

indicators.note: the phrase knocks back, swallows, the wine, so it sits inside the words

blocks.note: ontaRIO JAnitor

explanation.surface: A Canadian caretaker is drinking the red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' tempts a solver to read backwards, but the word runs forwards across 'Ontario janitor'; knocking back here means drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by the question mark: a Spanish red wine is one instance of 'the red'.

clue.text: Professor’s vulgar tweet

indicators.note: a professor lectures, so we hear the word as he says it

blocks.note: cheap = vulgar, tawdry

explanation.surface: An academic posts something crude on social media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweet' suggests social media, but it is a bird's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in the original sense: the small high note a young bird makes.

clue.text: His Majesty on dope? That’s silly

blocks.note: CR is Carolus Rex, King Charles
a dope is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of the King taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' is not drugs but a fool. In a down clue 'on' puts the king above the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: grossly stupid or insensitive, a stronger word than silly.

clue.text: Beg Penny to go first

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for penny
to lead is to go first

explanation.surface: Someone asks a woman called Penny to go ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name, but it is the coin, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to ask earnestly.

clue.text: Trousers lost by launderette finally turned up

indicators.note: things lost are all over the place, not in their proper order
only the final letter of launderette is taken

blocks.note: anagram fodder
the last letter of launderette

explanation.surface: Trousers lost at the launderette have at last reappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads as the lost trousers being found, but it is the definition, a turned-up nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A French loan word, used almost only of a nose that tilts up at the tip.

clue.text: Blunt anxious after change of heart

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word for anxious is changed

blocks.note: tense = anxious

explanation.surface: A blunt person turns anxious after changing their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says only that the heart changes, not what to; the new middle letter comes from the definition and crossers.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: brief to the point of rudeness.

clue.text: Attend to speech

blocks.note: the verb, as in dealing with a problem
the noun, a formal talk to an audience

explanation.walkthrough: 'To' looks like the link to 'speech', but it belongs to the first definition, a phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a verb for dealing with something and a noun for a formal talk.

clue.text: Pass festival on way north

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards

blocks.note: Eid is a Muslim festival

explanation.surface: Someone drives past a festival on the road north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' reads as going by, but it is passing away.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism: 'pass', short for 'pass away', is a gentle way of saying it.

clue.text: Others eclipsing heavyweight once, no dreamer he

indicators.note: the others eclipse the boxer by covering him

blocks.note: the rest = the others
Muhammad Ali, former heavyweight boxing champion

explanation.surface: Rivals outshine a former heavyweight, who is no dreamer himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase at the end: someone who is no dreamer.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by opposite: the dreamer's antonym, someone who sees things as they are.

clue.text: Be careful, young man

blocks.note: an exclamation of warning, as to someone about to fall
a dated word for a regular boyfriend

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the clue sounds like a warning to a youth; it is two definitions, an interjection and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a cautionary interjection, and old-fashioned slang for the boy someone is going out with.

clue.text: Badly cut English lady’s clothing

indicators.note: the clothing of lady is its outside, its first and last letters

blocks.note: to sever is to cut
E is the abbreviation for English
the outer letters of lady

explanation.surface: An English lady's clothes have been poorly tailored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly cut' reads as poor tailoring, but 'Badly' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in the sense of degree: badly hurt and severely hurt mean the same.
